title: Christianization of Kievan Rus'
summary: In 988 Prince Vladimir of Kyiv was baptised, married a Byzantine princess and made Orthodox Christianity the official religion of Rus'; the people of Kyiv were baptised en masse in the Dnieper. Churches replaced pagan idols and the children of leading families were sent to learn to read. Byzantine missions had worked in Rus' since the 860s. The conversion tied Rus' to Byzantium and Christian Europe, and Kyiv's St Sophia was built to rival Constantinople's. It shaped the later Russian, Ukrainian and Belarusian peoples.

uncertainty.note: Dated to 988 CE in the medieval Primary Chronicle for Vladimir's baptism and the baptism of the populace of Kyiv.

as_recorded.value: The Orthodox Church was brought to Kievan Rus’ in 988, when Prince Vladimir converted to Christianity, and established it as the official religion of Rus’
evangelized after the baptism of St Vladimir in 988

importance.justification: Brought the East Slavs into Orthodox Christianity, shaping the religion and culture of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus to this day (R3 D3 T4 L2).
